question: How would you design a real-time collaborative rich-text editor like Google Docs from a frontend perspective?
shortAnswer: Designing Google Docs requires four core pillars: 1) Conflict resolution using CRDTs (e.g. Yjs) or Operational Transformation (OT), 2) Bi-directional WebSocket communication with offline delta syncing via IndexedDB, 3) Custom layout rendering engine (migrated from DOM to Canvas/WebAssembly for exact pagination), and 4) Presence and awareness indicators (multi-cursor rendering).

When multiple users type in the same document simultaneously, standard DOM textareas cannot handle conflicts.

Google Docs breaks text into mathematical operations (Insert, Delete, Retain).

Using **CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types)**, edits merge deterministically on every user's screen without a central lock.
